title: ARIA tooltips need an accessible name
summary: An element with role tooltip has no accessible name, so it conveys nothing. Put the tooltip text inside it or add aria-label.
problem: An element with role="tooltip" has no accessible name. A tooltip gets its name from its content, so an empty tooltip, or one holding only an icon, gives assistive technology nothing to announce.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users who focus the control the tooltip describes hear no extra help. The hint exists only for people who can see it.
steps: Find the tooltip element in the scan result.
Put the hint text inside the tooltip element, so its content is the name.
If the tooltip is filled by script, check that the text is present when it is shown.
Connect it to its trigger with aria-describedby, and keep the tooltip reachable on keyboard focus as well as on hover.
after: Codes are on your order confirmation email.
whyItMatters: Tooltip text often holds guidance people need to complete a task. If it is empty for assistive technology, those users go without. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Select the tooltip in your browser's accessibility inspector and check that its Name is set. Focus the trigger with the keyboard and confirm the hint is available.
